title: Federated Learning with Only Positive Labels

pse.problem: Limitation in federated learning when each user has access to primarily or solely positive training examples associated with a limited number of classes
pse.solution_function: Learning a multi-class classification model in a federated learning setting by performing spreadout regularization to enable learning from users with only positive labels for limited classes, without allowing communication between users or access to other users' class parameters.
pse.solution_structure: System consists of distributed devices (user devices such as smartphones), a server, and neural networks. The user devices hold local data samples, the server facilitates iterative training by keeping track of a global model.
pse.solution_implementation:
During each round of the training process: 
1. Server sends the current global model to a set of participating users.
2. Each user updates the model with its local data and computes the logits for the instance x as Wg(x), where W is the classification matrix learned by the user.
3. Users send the model delta to the server, who averages (via Federated Averaging) the deltas collected from the participating users and updates the global model.
pse.effect: Leverages computational power of edge devices, reduces necessity of sending user data to server, improves trust/security, privacy, and fairness in federated learning scenarios with limited positive labels
